claim: More than one glass is grammatically singular despite denoting a plurality.
evidence_summary: Singular glass persists in the comparison. The alternation of no and none supplies an independent head test.
finding: The chapter distinguishes plurality of reference from grammatical singular in [6i]. Footnote 49 uses no/none in a separate construction with pre-head modification of more.
inference: Can plurality of reference determine grammatical number inside more than one glass?

evidence.passage: §11, p. 432. More than one glass is grammatically singular despite denoting a plurality.
evidence.example: More than one glass can describe two or more glasses, although glass takes singular form. In [6i] the whole subject also takes singular was. Footnote 49 gives a distinct headship argument for more with a pre-head modifier.
evidence.establishes: The chapter’s distinction between formal singular and semantic plurality survives this comparison.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
